We built an app nobody used.

When we launched Rotaship, we were proud of it. Sleek, modern, exactly what a mobile app should look like. We figured restaurant staff would pick it up and love it.

They didn't. In the first month, only 12% of staff even opened it.

That stung. But it taught us something worse: we weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we killed our own app and moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets now run on it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

1,000 families.

14 months ago, Pebble Pantry was an idea I scribbled down during maternity leave, sleep-deprived and staring at an empty fridge at 7pm.

Today, 1,000 families pay €4.99 a month to make dinner time a little easier.

We didn't get here through ad campaigns or growth hacks. Most of our families found us through school WhatsApp groups, parents recommending us to other parents.

That's trust, and it means more than any marketing budget.

To every mum and dad who shared us in a group chat: thank you. You built this with us.

To every founder building on a shoestring: keep going. Your community is your superpower.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

Why we stopped billing by the hour

When we started Fernway Studio, we did what every agency does: we charged hourly. 4 of our first 6 projects went over budget, clients were frustrated, and so were we.

So in 2024 we switched to a fixed price: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. Clients know exactly what they're paying, and we're incentivized to work smarter rather than longer.

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

They walked away 5 months in. It stung. A lot.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson? Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough.

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build. You just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

Every single wedding meant losing most of a day to culling. Clicking, comparing, deleting, repeat. Countless Mondays gone.

I loved capturing love stories. I didn't love the endless hours in front of Lightroom.

So I built Halftone. In testing, it culled 3,000 photos in 6 minutes. Six minutes.

It now lives right inside Lightroom Classic for $15/month, so photographers can spend less time sorting and more time shooting.

To every photographer who's ever sacrificed their weekend to the cull: this one's for you.
